subject: Week 26: half-year mark — convert swim to paid and call ISR now
bodyText:
This week
Avi's 6-month birthday lands Wednesday, Nov 11. The CDC 6-month checklist reads: rolls tummy-to-back, pushes up on straight arms, leans on hands when sitting; takes vocal turns, blows raspberries, squeals; reaches for what he wants and closes his lips to end a meal. Sleep is consolidated for many by now — if nights are still fragmented, this is a reasonable second window for sleep training.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Drool surge and mouthing everything — often, not always, upstream of a first tooth.
- [monitor] No babbling, no rolling in either direction, or no weight-bearing on legs when held upright — raise any of these at the 6-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Fever persisting past 24 hours, or lethargy out of proportion to a mild illness.
- [call now] Seizure activity, unresponsiveness, or blue lips — 911, not the nurse line.

Enrichment opportunities
- Convert swim to exactly one paid weekly class now that the free tier has ended: La Petite Baleen rolls into paid tuition at 6 months ($130-138/mo plus $50/yr registration, perpetual enrollment, auto-billing), JCCSF Water Babies runs $185-230/mo with waitlists capped at five (check actively for open slots rather than queueing), and SF Rec & Parks parent-tot runs under $10/session but demands registration-day execution. One program only — there is no dose-response evidence for swim under 12 months. La Petite Baleen tuition: https://www.swimlpb.com/swim-classes/tuition
- If ISR self-rescue is on the roadmap — strongest case for households with pool or regular water exposure — contact certified instructors this month: eligibility starts at 6 months plus unassisted sitting, but the nearest instructors (Mill Valley, Orinda, Walnut Creek) book 6-12 months out, so calling now targets a realistic start at 12-18 months. Evidence is case-series only; treat it as drowning-risk mitigation, not enrichment. Infant Swimming Resource: https://www.infantswim.com/
- Hand him an egg shaker or soft maraca — rhythm production, not just consumption, is the active ingredient in the infant music literature. Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Protect 60+ min/day of open floor play at his level — it outperforms any container and is the cheapest motor input available. AAP: Movement 4-7 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-4-to-7-Months.aspx
- Alternate the fixed bedtime book with a rotating library stack — repetition anchors the routine, novelty feeds vocabulary. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26–Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit window closes Monday, Nov 9 — if the visit has not happened, book the make-up now and hold the flu dose-two timing (four weeks after dose one).
- Day 180-240: Suzuki decision window — instrument choice, Book 1 recordings, teacher waitlists. Full brief next week.
- Nov 26, 2026: first Thanksgiving — if you are flying, book the infant-in-arms ticket now and plan feeds around ascent and descent.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Responds to other people's emotional expressions
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-others-emotions/complete

- Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/distinguishes-emotion-tone/complete

- Finds a partially hidden object
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/finds-partially-hidden-object/complete

- Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/struggles-for-out-of-reach/complete

- Begins to respond to the word 'no'
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-no/complete
